page: Amazon Web Services c5a.24xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by AMD EPYC 7R32 processors. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 96 virtual CPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The underlying infrastructure is managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile characterized by strong multi-threaded and specialized execution capabilities alongside weaker single-core performance. The instance registers in the bottom 10% for stress-ng single-core CPU performance, a limitation reflected in average single-threaded gzip and bzip3 decompression speeds. However, it excels in parallelized and instruction-heavy workloads. The passmark CPU encryption test ranks in the top 10%, while passmark CPU extended instructions, Geekbench software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing all place in the top 25%. Memory performance is highly efficient for cached operations, with small-block read-only bandwidth reaching 4497.3 GB/sec, though large-block uncached read and write speeds remain average.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c5a.24xlarge offers a high-density compute profile without the added expense of bundled local SSDs or GPU accelerators. This makes it a resource-efficient option for compute-heavy tasks that do not require high-speed local storage. The instance is highly suited for multi-threaded processing tasks such as software compilation, cryptography, image processing, and ray tracing. It also supports moderate database operations and Redis deployments, as evidenced by its strong performance of 83.89 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks, though it is less optimal for single-threaded applications or workloads requiring high per-core clock speeds.

It is configured with 192.0 GB of DDR4 RAM, a 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and runs on the Nitro hypervisor, with no local storage or GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks show a tradeoff: single-core performance is relatively weak, placing in the bottom 10% for stress-ng, whereas multi-threaded and specialized tasks perform exceptionally well. Notably, the instance achieves top-tier results in CPU encryption and strong marks in software compilation, ray tracing, and cached memory bandwidth. This profile makes the c5a.24xlarge highly cost-efficient for parallelized compute workloads, cryptography, and image processing, while being less suited for single-threaded applications.
